recipes.name: Strawberry Pretzel Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Stir crushed pretzels, melted butter, and 3 tablespoons sugar together until well-combined; mix well and press mixture into the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until set, about 8 to 10 minutes; set aside to cool.
Place cream cheese and 1 cup sugar in a large bowl. Beat with an electric mixer until smooth; fold in whipped topping. Spread mixture onto cooled crust.

Dissolve gelatin in boiling water. Stir in still-frozen strawberries and allow to set for a few minutes, until the mixture "looks like egg whites." Spoon and spread over cream cheese layer; refrigerate until set, at least 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Pretzel Salad
raw_recipe.description: Strawberry pretzel salad is the perfect crowd-pleasing dessert featuring a crunchy pretzel crust with a creamy filling and sweet strawberry layer on top.

review.reviewBody: My aunt has been making this recipe for years & has given me a few pointers....as Hollyfae said, be sure & make sure your cream cheese is all the way to the edges of the pan & sealed (to keep the jello from seeping under the cream cheese & making the crust soggy). It's also helpful to chill the cream cheese really well before topping w/ the jello. Sometimes I like to add an 8 oz. can of crushed pineapple in w/ the strawberries (Paula Deen's version)

SOME TIPS: This is an easy recipe to follow, but I can understand why people are having a problem with the layers. Thru my experience, this is what I did and didnt seem to have a problem with any of the layers seeping thru. FIRST-COOL THE CRUST COMPLETELY!! SECOND-CREAM THE SUGAR AND CREAM CHEESE THOROUGHLY! SPREAD ON PRETZEL MIXTURE AND REFRIGERATE AT LEAST 30-45 MINUTES. PREPARE JELLO AS DIRECTED BY DISSOLVING COMPLETELY FOR TWO MINUTES AND ADD FROZEN, SLICED STRAWBERRIES. LET SIT FOR ABOUT 5 MINUTES STIRRING FREQUENTLY DURING THOSE FIVE MINUTES UNTIL IT IS LIKE A JELLIED, SOFT TEXTURE. I USED A METAL WHISK TO ACCOMPLISH THIS. POUR OVER REFRIGERATED CREAM CHEESE LAYER. REFRIGERATE UNTIL SET, ABOUT A COUPLE OF HOURS. HOPE THIS HELPS!!!!

I love this recipe but found it much better if after the jello is all disolved I add 4 ice cubes until melted then add an 8 oz tub of whipped cream to the jello mixture and mix til smooth then adding the strawberries after. It stays more firm and has a wonderful creamy taste to it.

This was really fun to make. I only added just a little vanilla to the cream cheese/whipped topping layer. Other than that, I made no changes. I did follow other reviewer's suggestions and chill the layers in-between layering. Made for an easier time of layering. I also made sure to go right to the edges with the cream cheese layer to keep from the jello layer from seeping through and making the "crust" soggy. Fun! EDITED NEXT DAY: I LOVED the top and bottom layers. They were wonderful together. The bottom layer was.....just not right for this dessert. If I were to make this again, I'd double a recipe for graham cracker crust and use that instead of the pretzels. It just wasn't good. EDITED AGAIN A WEEK LATER: I made this again today with a crust made from Lorna Doone cookies. I just followed the same recipe, only using two sleeves of crushed Lorna Doone cookies. Much better.
EDITED YET AGAIN: I made the top layer today with Blackberry Fusion Jello and this summer's blackberries. Fabulous. Not as overpoweringly sweet as the strawberries.

I followed this recipe exactly, except that I mixed up the jello, boiling water and frozen strawberries and let it sit at room tempeature for 30 minutes while the crust and cream cheese layer chilled. Then I let the whole dessert chill overnight. I also only baked the crust for 8 minutes. This is a very tasty recipe and people absolutely love it.

Also good with Raspberry gelatin and use frozen raspberries....not in juice, just frozen. I also use 1/2 cup of powdered sugar rather than 1 cup of sugar....it's plenty sweet. The cream cheese layer does need to be chilled for about 45-60 minutes and I chill the gelatin for about 40 minutes then add the frozen berries....pour that onto the cheese layer. It is a great potluck recipe.
Love this recipe & I get requests for it all the time. Make sure to spread the cream cheese mixture all the way to the edges - it keeps the jello from making the crust mushy. Thanks Betty!

Here is what I did different for the crust: 2½ cups pretzels, crushed 2 teaspoons vanilla extract ⅔ cup brown sugar 2 tablespoons flour ½ cup butter, melted Mix together and bake at 375 for 10 minutes. Cool Completely. I found that the crust holds together better.

Love this recipe - but I substituted and heated pineapple juice to make the jello (instead of water) - that was Yummy. And also increased and made 1.5 times the recipe for the pretzel crust. (using 3 cups). Important: Be sure to follow the recipe here and only use "2 Cups" of liquid TOTAL to dilute your 6 oz of jello. If you follow jello box instructions which would be double that, then it will be thin and not set up well. Also by adding the strawberries straight out of the freezer, the jello mixture thickens and sets up super fast. No waiting. It will start to gel up in just a few minutes on the counter.

This is fantastic and so easy to make! I took the advice of other reviewers and made sure each layer was cooled before adding the next and I made sure the whipped topping layer went all the way to the edges of the dish. Everything was perfect! The pretzel crust was still crunchy even after three days of being in the refrigerator so this dessert would be a great one to make ahead. I'm on my second time making this and, at the last minute, I decided to add a small can of crushed pineapple to the strawberries, as someone suggested is the way Paula Dean makes it and it was so delicious. Perfect blend of flavors. The next time I make this, I will try cutting the pretzel crust into serving-size squares before it completely cools so when the toppings are on it and it's ready to serve, the crust will already be cut for easy and quick servings. Also, I might quarter the strawberries vs using halves like I did just because I don't love biting into big pieces of fruit. However, everything was great exactly as the recipe is written. You can't go wrong! It's a definite keeper! Thanks for sharing!

This is always a hit when I make it! I also have made it with orange jello and mandarin oranges, very good too! Make sure you crush the pretzels well! Also, make sure the cream cheese layer is spread to all sides and corners and there are no holes! I do find that putting the dish in the refrigerator between layers helps it to set nicely!
This was a crowd favorite. The only difference was that I made whipped cream instead of using cool whip and it turned out great.

Do not wait until the jello is slightly set "like egg whites" to add to the topping. You run the risk of waiting slightly too long and the jello will start to set and instead of smooth top you will have chunky jello mixed with strawberries. Adding the frozen strawberries to the jello cools it down almost immediately to a temperature that you can safely add to the cool whip layer.
It was really too sweet. I don't think its necessary to add suger to pretzels and to the cream cheese filling. I did not care for it.

I have made this for years, but in the past few years I now have a mess when I try to get it out of the glass baking dish! I have not changed a thing. My recipe is exactly as this one. I did have a better outcome when I used a metal 9x13 inch cake pan.
Made this for Easter and a party. A big hit every time.

I have made this three times and I love the taste, but I have problems with the crust... Does anyone else? Temp is fine, time is fine I am not burning. I am crushing them up good., I even tried more pretzels and more butter but it's sooo crumbly. I changed my review because this time the jello didn't set. I think there are too many factors that could go wrong with this. My first time was pretty good but this time... Maybe it was because it was generic jello, who knows..
Best easy desert

I love this recipe! It is so delicious and easy to make. I use whatever pretzels I have in the house, especially cinnamon sugar pretzels and honey mustard. Gives the crust really good flavor. Absolutely a crowd pleaser!!!
I loved this, but I did make fresh whipping cream!!
